tips.title: Removing Old Paint From Plastic Kits
tips.text: Use Tamiya Plastic Cement to dissolve old paint on plastic kits. Apply a thin layer to the painted area, let it sit 10 minutes, then gently scrape with a dental tool. For stubborn areas, mix 1:1 Tamiya Cement with Mr. Hobby's Acrylic Thinner and apply with a brush. Wipe with a damp cloth to remove residue. Avoid prolonged exposure to prevent warping. Always test on an inconspicuous area first. For detailed parts, use a fine-tipped tool to carefully lift paint without damaging the plastic.

tips.title: Fixing Broken Photo-Etch Parts
tips.text: Use Iwata’s Precision Clamp to hold broken photo-etch parts together. Apply a drop of Tamiya Plastic Cement to the fracture site, then press firmly. For delicate parts, use a small amount of CA glue (e.g., Tamiya CA) and gently bend the broken section into place. Allow to cure fully. If the part is too fragile, use a fine sanding stick to shape and smooth the joint. Always work in a well-lit area to ensure proper alignment.

tips.title: Recovering Clogged Airbrushes
tips.text: For clogged Iwata airbrushes, disassemble and soak the nozzle in Tamiya’s Airbrush Cleaner for 10 minutes. Use a soft brush to clear residue. For stubborn blockages, soak the nozzle in 70% isopropyl alcohol for 15 minutes. Rinse thoroughly with water, then prime with Tamiya’s Airbrush Primer before using. Always clean the airbrush after each session to prevent future clogs. Use a 2.5mm nozzle for fine details and adjust pressure to 10-15 psi for optimal flow.

tips.title: Avoiding Frost From Rattle Cans
tips.text: Frost on rattle cans (like Microscale or Clear Prop Models) occurs from excess moisture. To prevent it, store cans in a dry, temperature-controlled environment. If frost appears, use a heat gun on low heat to melt it, then wipe clean. For stubborn frost, apply a small amount of Tamiya’s Paint Thinner to the can’s surface and let it sit for 5 minutes. Always use a thin spray coat to avoid condensation buildup. Store cans upright to minimize moisture contact.

tips.title: Fixing Paint Reactions/Bubbling
tips.text: Paint reactions or bubbling (e.g., from Vallejo Model Air and AK Interactive) often result from thinning or improper application. To fix, gently sand the affected area with 600-grit wet sandpaper, then apply a thin layer of Tamiya’s Sealant to seal the surface. For bubbles, use a pin to pierce them and apply Tamiya’s Clear Primer to fill the void. Always test new paints on a separate panel for compatibility. Avoid over-spraying; use a spray gun with a 2.5mm nozzle for even coverage.
